research.approach: Practitioners treat an Amazon rank drop as a diagnosis problem before any fix. They first verify the drop and date it (a cliff points to a stock-out or suppression, a slow slide to decay), then check the account and listing for suppression, the Featured Offer (Buy Box), stock and price changes. They line up every listing edit, including image and keyword changes, against the drop date, split the loss into traffic versus conversion, and look at competitors and ads. Only then do they change one thing at a time, defend the main keyword with ads within a cap, and give a recovery weeks to show, because rank returns slowly. Main image tests need enough traffic and run for weeks, so a quick revert and a slow test cannot both happen in the same window.

sources.title: SellerSprite: Diagnosing a sudden drop in keyword ranking
sources.note: Ordered diagnosis: verify the drop and its shape, check inventory, price and promotions, competitors, then listing changes including main image changes and click-through. Warns against abruptly pausing ads. Tool vendor blog.

sources.title: Bellavix: Amazon sales drop, how to diagnose and recover lost sales
sources.note: Diagnostic order: market demand, account health and suppression, traffic, conversion (price, listing, negative reviews), inventory and Featured Offer; recovery steps including ads and stock-outs. Agency blog.

sources.title: Seller Labs: Manage Your Experiments, A/B testing listings the right way
sources.note: Main image tests need Brand Registry and enough traffic, change one thing, run 8 to 10 weeks or to significance (at least about four weeks), apply a winner only at about 95% confidence. Vendor knowledge base.

sources.title: Amazon margins, stock and claim review

steps.name: Verify the drop and date it
steps.why: Rank moves a few places naturally. A cliff points to stock or suppression, a slide to decay; whether all keywords fell or one decides where to look.

steps.name: Put every change on one timeline against the drop date
steps.why: The main image change, price and coupon changes, stock-outs, the 1-star review and ad changes all sit near the drop. Without dates, the wrong one gets blamed.

steps.name: Check suppression, Featured Offer and account health
steps.why: A suppressed listing or lost Buy Box is a same-day fix and explains a cliff. It must be ruled out before looking at content.

steps.name: Split the loss into traffic and conversion
steps.why: Fewer sessions means rank and visibility; fewer purchases per session means price, listing or reviews. The fix differs.

steps.name: Read competitors, reviews and ads
steps.why: A competitor with heavy ads or a lower price can take the slot; a damaging photo review hits conversion; ads show whether the main keyword is still defended.

steps.name: Fix one cause at a time and defend the keyword within the cap
steps.why: Several simultaneous changes cannot be attributed. Ads on the main keyword help rank recover but must stay under the $120 cap and be wound down gradually.

steps.name: Decide whether to revert the main image or test it
steps.why: A main image test needs weeks and traffic; with six weeks to recover, a revert is quicker, a test is cleaner. The owner chooses and the date is logged.

steps.name: Read recovery weekly against rank, units and spend
steps.why: Rank returns over one to several weeks. A weekly read on the same definitions shows whether a change worked or something else moved.

pitfalls.text: Blaming the main image or the 1-star review because they are visible, without checking stock, price and Buy Box on the drop date.
Changing the image, title and ads together so the result cannot be attributed.
Pausing or cutting ads abruptly, which lowers sales velocity and can deepen the rank loss.
Ending a main image test early because early results look good, or applying a low-confidence result.
Trying to remove or incentivise reviews in ways that break Amazon policy and risk suppression.

stages.name: Pin down the problem
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured problem, a target, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Gather the sales, traffic, ads and change history
stages.goal: Pull 90 days of daily sales and traffic, Sponsored Products reports, inventory and listing history, the 1-star review and a competitor snapshot into CSV files in the project.

checks.name: Covers at least 30 days before the drop and the weeks since
Daily units match the 60 to 30 the owner reported, or the difference is explained
Missing items (rank history, change dates, unit cost) are listed rather than assumed

stages.name: Verify the drop and build the timeline
stages.goal: Confirm the drop is real, find its date and shape (cliff or slide, one keyword or all), and put the image change, price, coupon, stock, review, competitor and ad events on one dated timeline.

checks.name: The drop date is found from organic sessions and units, and from rank history if there is any
Every change near the drop has a date and a source, or is marked unknown
The loss is split into sessions versus conversion, before and after the drop
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for diagnosis

stages.name: Check the listing is healthy and eligible
stages.goal: Rule out suppression, lost Featured Offer, stock-outs, account health issues and a non-compliant main image, so content causes are only blamed when these are clear.

checks.name: Suppressed status, account health and policy notices are checked or marked not seen
Featured Offer percentage and stock are compared with the drop date
The current main image is checked against Amazon's main image rules

stages.name: Find what is driving the rank and sales loss
stages.goal: Test each hypothesis against the timeline, traffic and conversion split, competitors, review and ad data. Keep competing explanations; the main image and the 1-star review are tested, not assumed.

checks.name: Every listed hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with evidence
Each supported cause is shown to have happened before the drop, not only near it
Each main finding names a competing explanation
Conversion findings meet a minimum number of sessions, or are marked low-confidence

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked cards: for example revert or test the main image, restore keyword terms, restructure Sponsored Products inside $120 a day, respond to the review. Each card gives expected effect on units, effort, risk and how it will be measured, and what must not be changed together.

checks.name: Every card cites the finding it rests on
Every card has expected direction, effort, confidence, risk and how it will be measured
No card needs more than $120 a day in Sponsored Products spend
Cards that would confuse each other are sequenced, not bundled, and the six-week window is respected
No card incentivises or tries to remove reviews outside Amazon's rules

stages.name: Owner chooses
stages.goal: The owner picks card IDs, including whether to revert the main image or test it. Ask for the reason when they pass on a top card; record it as a decision.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over cards are recorded
A reason is recorded wherever the top card was passed over

stages.name: Prepare the listing changes
stages.goal: Prepare the chosen listing changes: restore or test the main image, put back any removed high-volume keyword in the title or bullets, and draft a public reply to the 1-star review if the owner chose that. Each change comes with exact steps and the old value for undo.

checks.name: Only chosen changes are included, one per step, each with the finding it answers
The current value of everything changed is saved so it can be put back
The main image and the copy follow Amazon's image and claims rules

stages.name: Prepare the Sponsored Products changes
stages.goal: Prepare the chosen ad changes within $120 a day: defend "garlic press" and its close terms, cut search terms that spend without selling, and move budget between campaigns. Written as steps or a bulk sheet for the owner to apply.

checks.name: Planned daily spend across all campaigns never exceeds $120
Cuts to existing campaigns are gradual, not an abrupt pause
Each change has a stop rule on cost per sale and a date to review

stages.name: Owner applies each change, one at a time
stages.goal: Register each change as a test with its metric and review date, then hand the owner one change at a time to make in Seller Central. Record the date and what was changed, and check the live listing.

checks.name: Each change is registered with its date, expected effect and review date before it is applied
Listing changes that could affect the same metric are spaced out
The owner confirms each change is live and we check the public listing

stages.name: Read recovery weekly
stages.goal: Each week, read daily units, sessions, conversion, keyword rank, ad spend and cost per sale from fresh exports against the baseline and each registered change, and check the guardrails.

checks.name: Weeks are compared on the same definitions and dates, and weekday mix is allowed for
A result is credited to a change only if no other change landed in the same window
Daily ad spend against $120 and profit per unit are checked

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close each change with a verdict, record what caused the drop and what recovered it, propose rules for future listing changes, and plan the next round if 55 units a day is not yet reached.

checks.name: Every applied change has a verdict
Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this product, this brand or Amazon listings in general

hypotheses.statement: The rank drop is partly normal movement or a tool artefact, and sales fell for another reason.
hypotheses.test: Compare rank history with organic sessions and units by day; check whether all keywords fell or only the main one.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Organic sessions held while reported rank moved, or rank fell only after sales fell.
hypotheses.refute_if: Rank and organic sessions fell on the same days across keywords.

hypotheses.statement: The new main image lowered click-through or conversion and the rank followed.
hypotheses.test: Click-through and unit session percentage in the weeks before and after the image change, against the drop date.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Click-through or unit session percentage fell within days of the image change and before rank fell.
hypotheses.refute_if: Click-through and conversion held after the change and the fall began later for another reason.

hypotheses.statement: The 1-star review with photos is putting buyers off and lowering conversion.
hypotheses.test: Unit session percentage by day around the review date; what the review and photos show; whether they were shown near the top of the reviews.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Conversion fell soon after the review appeared and the review describes a fault buyers can see.
hypotheses.refute_if: Conversion did not move when the review appeared.

hypotheses.statement: A stock-out, price or coupon change, or a lost Featured Offer cut sales and rank.
hypotheses.test: Stock logs, price and coupon history and Featured Offer percentage lined up with the drop date.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Any of them changed within about 48 hours before the drop.
hypotheses.refute_if: Stock, price and Featured Offer were stable through the drop.

hypotheses.statement: The listing is suppressed or has an account health or policy issue.
hypotheses.test: Suppressed status in inventory, account health page and policy notices; main image compliance.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A suppression, notice or non-compliant image is found around the drop date.
hypotheses.refute_if: The listing is active with no notices.

hypotheses.statement: A competitor with lower price, heavy ads or more reviews took the page-one slots.
hypotheses.test: Compare current page-one competitors' price, rating, review count and image with ours, and when new ones appeared.
hypotheses.confirm_if: One or more competitors are cheaper or newly promoted while our metrics held.
hypotheses.refute_if: Competitors are unchanged and our own conversion fell.

hypotheses.statement: Sponsored Products spend of $90 a day is not defending the main keyword and wastes budget on weak terms.
hypotheses.test: Search term and targeting reports: spend and orders on "garlic press" and close terms versus terms that spend without selling.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The main keyword gets little of the spend, or a large share goes to terms with no orders.
hypotheses.refute_if: The main keyword is well covered and efficient.

hypotheses.statement: Demand for garlic presses fell across the category, not just for this listing.
hypotheses.test: Compare our sessions with competitors' visible movement and, if available, category search volume trend over the same weeks.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Competitors and search volume also fell in the same weeks.
hypotheses.refute_if: Category demand is steady while ours fell.

measurement.window: Weekly for six weeks from the first change, comparing like-for-like weeks and each registered change's start date.
measurement.min_volume: Judge conversion only on at least 300 sessions per period; otherwise report INCONCLUSIVE. Daily units are read as a seven-day average.
measurement.stop_rule: Stop and reverse a change early only if daily ad spend would pass $120, profit per unit turns negative, or the listing is suppressed; otherwise read the full week before judging.
